subject: Minke example - combining variances and getting  LCL and UCL for full stratification

messages.author: 1e2e7927fc1dbf3d
messages.subject: Minke example - combining variances and getting  LCL and UCL for full stratification
parts:
I am trying to see how to combine the variances in the full stratification (independent samples)   model of the Minke whale vignette.

My thinking thus far is that since the model is independent, we can treat the strata as independent random variables and do the following

SE (A+B) = sqrt ( SE(A)^2 + SE(B)^2 )   since there is no covariance term because of independence. 

I can then calculate the CV = SE/MU  ;  so far so good.

Now I would like to get the LCL and UCL for the total as well.  I'm not quite sure how to get there.  I thought about the delta method, but I'm not sure how to implement it here.

Finally, I would like to calculate the correct df --- this may be a precondition of the LCL and UCL, if we are using a df based CI calculation (chisq or t)

Good morning David

Glad to see you are making good progress with your duplication of uncertainty calculations.  I'm travelling today, so I can't give your question my full attention.  However, as you note, computing the confidence interval bounds does depend upon calculation of degrees of freedom.

The R package Distance, as well as Distance for Windows uses the Satterthwaite method to calculate degrees of freedom.  This is described in Section 3.6.1 of Buckland et al. (2001) duplicated below:


With the minke dataset, there is a CV associated with encounter rate, a CV associated with fitting the detection function, so "q" in the formula above is equal to 2.

Note too that confidence interval bounds in distance sampling are based on the assumption that the sampling distribution of the estimates of density are log-normally distributed, with a long right tail.  Consequently, the confidence intervals are asymmetrical.  Those calculations are described in the same section of Buckland et al.
